Autocomplete broke because the language server behind it, `piton lsp`, is no longer running in your copy of Suspense. The app never noticed it had stopped. I've fixed that part: the app now restarts the server when it stops. I haven't found what made it stop.

**What I found**
- **Your app:** the Suspense you're running has no `piton lsp` process under it; the only one is the `claude` run for this prompt. Without the server, completion requests quietly come back empty.
- **Why it stayed broken:** the app threw away the server's error output and didn't restart it when it exited, so it stayed dead until you restarted the app or reopened the project.
- **Not reproduced:** I couldn't make the server crash. In tests, completion works even when typing at full speed with real keystrokes inside the main window. A fresh server also survived your exact prompt typed one character at a time, and opening every spec file, including the new ones with import cycles. Since your app's server started, what killed it is unknown.

**The fix** (`src/project_lsp.rs`, `src/piton_lsp.rs`)
- **Restart:** a server that stops on its own is started again a second later. The chat input and editor already reconnect whenever the server changes, so completions come back by themselves.
- **Logging:** when the server stops, the app prints how it stopped and the last 40 lines of the server's error output to its own stderr. If it happens again, that should show why.
- **Crash loops:** after 3 failures in a row, each within 10 seconds of starting, it gives up until the project is opened again.
- **Spec:** there's a new "stopping" section in `LSP` (`spec/scope/lsp/index.pi`).

A new test kills the real server: the first two times it checks that a new server comes up and completes `@{Appl`, and after the third it checks the server stays down until the project is reopened. The Piton checks and `piton build` passed.

**To get autocomplete back now:** restart Suspense. Your running copy is `target/release/suspense` from 04:52, so run `cargo build --release` first to pick up the restart fix.
